title: Experiment deployment orchestra - steward scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational-first scratchpad for coordinating cross-functional experiments, progressive exposure, and canary choreography for LLM-powered routes. This is intentionally informal — quick rituals, decision heuristics, small checklists, and rehearsal notes to reduce friction between Eng / Product / SRE / CS when we ship changes that touch inference behavior, routing, or model selection.

Audience:
- Release stewards (rotation)
- Product owners running A/B or progressive rollouts
- Oncall SREs and Observability lead
- Solutions engineers / CS for customer-impacting test slices

High-level intent:
- Make a 1-page steward playbook for low-friction rollouts (canary -> expand -> rollback) that fits into the Console rollout flow.
- Emphasize human-in-the-loop checks at key exposure gates, not just automated signals.
- Embed cost and latency safety nets (token budgets, tail latency thresholds) alongside quality metrics.

Quick protocol (5-minute read):
1) Preflight (owner): assign steward, list stakeholders, link tickets + eval set. Add to release calendar.
2) Canary launch (small slice): 0.5–2% traffic or synthetic traffic equivalent. Observe 30–60m.
3) Canary hold (steward): validate 3 signal buckets: infra (errors, latency, capacity), cost (tokens / model variant mix), quality (eval pass rate, A/B metrics, critical user flows).
4) Expand in factors (x2, x5, x10) with 15–60m holds. Each expansion requires steward sign-off.
5) Auto-fallback rules: if infra or cost signals breach thresholds, fallback to last stable model variant and pause exposures.
6) Postmortem trigger if rollback or if quality regressed > predefined delta.

Steward checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Confirm experiment hypothesis in title and primary metric (clear pass/fail).
- [ ] Linked eval prompt set (id) + expected behaviour notes.
- [ ] Synthetic load plan if user traffic < 5k req/day.
- [ ] Baseline telemetry snapshot (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, cost/tok).
- [ ] SLO/cost budget for the experiment (max incremental cost/day).
- [ ] Communication plan: slack channel, pager contacts, customer facing comms (if applicable).

Observation buckets & example heuristics:
- Infra: 5xx rate > 0.3% OR p99 latency increase > 40% vs baseline -> immediate pause and fallback.
- Cost: average token/unit cost delta > 25% and projected daily overrun > budget -> pause and escalate finance ops.
- Quality: primary metric regression > 2x minimum detectable effect (MDE) OR user critical flow failure seen in telemetry -> rollback.
- Safety signal (human): CS flags >= 3 instances from customers in the canary cohort -> hold and investigate.

Human-in-the-loop rituals (practical):
- Steward ritual 0: preflight quick sync (15m) with eng/product/obs.
- Steward ritual 1: canary watch (first hour) — steward ping at 15m, 30m, 60m with one-line status (ok/warn/block) and signal snapshot.
- Ritual 2: expansion gating call (5m) if any signal flagged. Do not expand without explicit ok.
- Ritual 3: post-expansion check-in 2h after reaching >=50% traffic.

Example orchestration matrix (mini):
- Change type: Model variant weight shift (same architecture) -> Lower infra risk, medium cost risk, medium quality risk.
- Change type: New decoding strategy (nucleus -> sampling variant) -> medium infra, low cost, medium-high quality risk.
- Change type: New reranker + reweighing -> high infra (latency), cost depends on reranker size, high quality risk.
Use matrix to pick canary size and synthetic traffic plan.

Synthetic rehearsals (when to use):
- Low-volume endpoints (< 2k/day) or enterprise-only features. Run traffic generator that mimics TTL/seq lengths of real traffic. Capture KV-cache warm-up effects.
- For caching-sensitive features, rehearse pre-warm scenarios where 10–20% synthetic repeat prefixes are used.

Signals dashboard (minimum):
- Token throughput and model mix by route (time series)
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route and model
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) by route
- Cost burn (projected vs budget) and per-request cost
- Primary metric delta and user flow success rate
- CS quick mentions (Slack thread count + flagged tickets)

Rollback taxonomy (fast vs careful):
- Fast rollback: immediate revert to previous model variant or route-level fallback. Triggered by infra or catastrophic quality failure.
- Careful rollback: gradually reweight traffic away from experiment and open a hold for deeper investigation (used when signal noisy or ambiguous).

Comms templates (short snippets for Slack / Release channel):
- Canary start: "Canary START: [experiment] | steward: Riley | slice: 1% | watch 60m | primary metric: conv-success-rate | links: JIRA RR-1254, eval set"
- Canary pause: "Canary PAUSE: [experiment] | reason: p99 latency +50% | steward: Riley | action: fallback to v23 (now)"
- Canary expand: "Canary EXPAND -> 5%: no infra or quality flags at 60m; steward approval @riley"

Open questions / outstanding decisions (TODO):
- What is the canonical naming convention for cohort slices in Console? (current chaos: cohort-1 / cohort-a / cust-123) -> propose standardized prefix: exp/{short-name}/{slice}.
- Should token budget gating be soft (alerts) vs hard (auto-pause)? Current leaning: hard pause for first 24h of a new experiment with >10% cost delta.
- How to surface CS tickets as a telemetry signal (automated flag from Zendesk?) — engineering effort required.

Playbook snippets to copy into Console docs later:
- Single-line gating rules (machine readable): "infra: p99>1.4x baseline OR error_rate>0.003 -> fallback"
- Steward rotation doc link: CONFLUENCE:steward-rotation-2025 (placeholder)

Mini postmortem template (if rollback or quality regression):
- What changed (config, model, infra)?
- Timeline of exposure/expansion/flags/rollback
- Primary root cause hypothesis + evidence 
- Immediate mitigations + longer-term fixes
- Owners for fixes and ETA

Notes to self (Riley):
- Revisit synthetic traffic generator to include token-length distribution sampling from prod in last 30d.
- Work with Observability to get delta-percent cards in Console for quick eye-balls.
- Talk to CS about a 1-click "flag as urgent" flow in Console for steward notifications.

Next steps (actionable):
- [Riley] Draft standard slice name proposal and post to #rollouts (due 2025-01-24).
- [Noah] Prototype a hard-pause token-budget rule for one non-critical experiment (due 2025-02-03).
- [Maya] Wire a lightweight Slack alert for CS-flagged tickets by experiment slice (POC by 2025-02-10).

End notes: This doc is intentionally messy — copy into a formal playbook when we stabilize conventions. Keep this as the tactical place for steward-run experiments until then.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-05: initial sketch by Riley
- 2024-12-12: added synthetic rehearsal checklist (Noah)
- 2025-01-18: token budget hard-pause suggestion added (Maya)
